examples.title: CI gate: reproducible, no encryption, safe names

description: Read-only archive report in ONE call: size, entry / file / directory counts, Zip64, comment, compressed vs uncompressed totals, per-method counts, encrypted / symlink / data-descriptor / Zip64 / cp437 / duplicate / unsafe-name counts, date range, a `determinism` verdict (epoch timestamps + canonical order + UTF-8 flags ⇒ reproducible; `canonicalLayout` = no data descriptors) and every engine diagnostic (prepended SFX data, name mismatches, …). Opens EAGERLY by default: every entry's real extent is checked up front — overlapping entries, entries reaching into the central directory or past EOF, and Zip64 spoofing — and refused with their ZIP_* code rather than summarised (a method / CRC / size divergence between central and local headers is caught by verify_zip and on read, not here). `check:[…]` / `assert:{…}` turn it into a CI gate → `checks[]` + `checksPassed`. Token-frugal: verbosity:'summary', fields:[…]. Input: zipBase64 or zipPath (sandbox).

access.description: 'auto' (default): in memory, and a zipPath above 1073741824 bytes by byte ranges. 'range': always by byte ranges over the sandbox file (never a URL; memory ≈ the central directory). 'memory': always buffered (INPUT_TOO_LARGE above the cap).

has.description: Entry names that must be present (exact).

maxEntries.description: The archive must hold at most this many entries.

maxUncompressedBytes.description: Sum of the declared uncompressed sizes must not exceed this.

method.description: Every entry must use this method.

minEntries.description: The archive must hold at least this many entries.

canonicalDate.description: The date the archive was canonicalised with (canonicalize_zip `date`, modify_zip `canonical.date`): the canonical-form verdict then expects that timestamp on every entry instead of the DOS epoch. Read as UTC, like every date this server writes.

check.description: CI assertions evaluated over the report: deterministic, epoch-timestamps, canonical-order, utf8-names, no-data-descriptor, canonical-layout, no-zip64, zip64, no-encryption, no-symlinks, safe-names, no-duplicates, no-diagnostics, store-only, deflate-only, and the engine's canonical form (canonical-form = zipnative's analyzeDeterminism verdict: epoch or pinned timestamps, canonical order, UTF-8 flags, Zip64-only extras, version-made-by 0x032D; canonical-extras; canonical-version-made-by). Result: `checks[]` + `checksPassed`.

determinismReport.description: true adds `determinismReport`: zipnative's analyzeDeterminism() verdict in full — the stricter canonical form canonicalize_zip produces (also Zip64-only extras and the constant version-made-by) and every offending entry with the rule it breaks.

fields.description: Dot-paths to keep, after verbosity (e.g. ['entryCount', 'entries.name']); unmatched ones are listed in _meta.unmatchedFields.

limits.description: Per-call override of zipnative's security bounds (CWE-400/409); absent keys keep the engine defaults (describe_engine.defaultLimits). A value above its operator ceiling is LIMIT_CEILING_EXCEEDED. Raise only for trusted input.

maxEntryCompressedSize.description: Bytes, one compressed payload fetched by the byte-range reader (access range).

strict.description: Turn the first engine diagnostic into a ZIP_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC error.

validate.description: 'eager' (default) cross-checks every local header and the overlap table up front — hostile shapes are refused here; 'lazy' defers to first read (cheaper on huge archives).

verbosity.description: 'summary': scalar verdict fields only (the token-frugal form).

zipBase64.description: Archive bytes, base64 (≤ 128 MiB decoded). Exclusive with zipPath.

zipPath.description: Archive path relative to the ZIPNATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR sandbox (container extensions: .zip .jar .docx .epub …). Exclusive with zipBase64; saves re-sending bytes between calls.

name: inspect_zip

outputSchema.description: Structured archive report (the zipnative inspect --json shape). Every property is optional because the result can be projected: verbosity:'summary' returns only the scalar summary fields, fields:[...] keeps a dot-path subset. Defaults return the full shape.

access.description: Present when the archive was read by byte ranges (access 'range', or a zipPath above the in-memory cap): `determinism` is then absent and the determinism checks fail with that reason.

canonicalLayout.description: summary only: buffered (no data descriptor) layout.

checksPassed.description: Present when check / assert was supplied: true when every assertion holds.

determinism.description: `deterministic` = reproducible (epoch timestamps + canonical order + UTF-8 flags); `canonicalLayout` = the buffered layout (no data descriptors) — a streamed archive is reproducible but not canonical.

determinismReport.description: Present with determinismReport: true — zipnative's analyzeDeterminism() report. `deterministic` here is the engine's canonical form (stricter than determinism.deterministic: also no extra field but Zip64 and version-made-by 0x032D).

canonicalExtras.description: No extra field other than Zip64 (0x0001) on any entry.

epochTimestamps.description: Every entry carries the DOS epoch, or the canonicalDate given.

offenders.description: Every broken rule, entry by entry, in central-directory order (at most 200 rows).

pinnedDate.description: The canonicalDate the timestamps were compared with (ISO-8601, UTC).

diagnosticCount.description: summary only: number of distinct diagnostics.

diagnostics.description: Non-fatal engine concerns (de-duplicated by code + entry, ≤ 200; codes in describe_engine.diagnosticCodes). Empty for a clean archive.

diagnosticsTruncated.description: true when rows beyond 200 were dropped.

isZip64.description: A Zip64 end-of-central-directory record is present.

prependedData.description: SFX-style prefix before the first local header (offsets shifted).

unsafeNameCount.description: Names sanitizeEntryPath() refuses (traversal, absolute, drive/UNC, NUL, ADS, device names).

title: Inspect archive (facts, determinism verdict, CI checks)
